verdict.rationale: Fly.io documents Sprites, persistent Linux VMs where agents keep running, checkpoint their state, and sleep until needed, so autonomous agents can live in the background. It does not document a first-party way to define automations, such as triggers or recurring schedules, and a community user says cron-like scheduling is missing from the platform, so users must build their own scheduler. Missing for 10: native scheduled/recurring automation, documented trigger or automation configuration, independent hands-on corroboration of background agent runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Every agent gets its own Linux box. A Sprite checkpoints itself while the agent works, so harnesses like Claude and Codex find everything where they left it.
Give it a Sprite that sleeps until it's needed and wakes up remembering everything.
For me the missing bit in Fly is scheduled tasks.
